patients.summary: Preschool teacher with type 1 diabetes since age 11 (outside endocrinology) and lifelong heavy periods who joins in 2019. Celiac disease with dermatitis herpetiformis surfaces in late 2022, bringing recurrent iron deficiency anemia needing IV iron and vitamin D deficiency; a right dacryocystitis in 2025; a first pregnancy ends in a planned cesarean for breech in June 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT, 25F, preschool teacher.

Here to set up primary care after a move; last PCP visit maybe two years ago, records requested.

T1DM since age 11. Followed by an outside endocrine group twice a year, uses pens, glargine 24 u at bedtime and lispro with meals by a correction scale. Checks fingersticks 4-5x/day. Last A1c she remembers was around 7. No severe lows, no DKA admissions as an adult. Has never been told of eye or kidney problems; gets a yearly eye exam.

GYN: periods have always been heavy, since about 14. Regular monthly, 6-7 days, first 3 days soak through a pad every couple of hours. Cramps managed with OTC ibuprofen 400 every 6 h for a day or two. Not sexually active with anyone but her partner, not planning pregnancy right now. Last Pap last year, normal per her.

Meds: glargine, lispro, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.
PMH: T1DM. PSH: none.
FH: father T1DM. Mother autoimmune thyroid disease. Maternal aunt with celiac.
SH: lives with partner. Never smoker. Alcohol a glass of wine a few times a year. No drugs. Works with 4-year-olds, walks most evenings.

ROS negative except heavy menses.

Exam: well appearing, vitals per flowsheet. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin: injection sites on abdomen without lipohypertrophy. Feet: intact sensation to monofilament, pulses 2+.

A/P
1. T1DM - stays with endocrinology, will request their notes. Urine microalbumin, lipids, CMP today. Yearly eye exam continues.
2. Heavy menses - longstanding, no anemia symptoms. CBC today. Ibuprofen as needed. Offered GYN eval, she declines for now, says it has always been this way.
3. Health maintenance: HIV/HCV once today. Pap due 2021 if last year's is confirmed normal. PHQ-2 negative. Flu shot in the fall.
RTC 1 yr for physical.

The HIV and hepatitis C screens are negative. Your old office sent your records and your Pap from last year was normal, so you're not due for another until 2021. See you next spring.

Meter download shows most readings in range, a few mild lows after afternoon recess duty that she treats herself. A1c today 7.1%. Feet normal. BP normal.
Medications: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, ibuprofen as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Plan: no basal change; small snack before afternoon outdoor time. Return in 6 months.
Regards,
Endocrinology

orders.reason: chronic loose stools, bloating, weight loss, vesicular rash

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is at home after school; identity and consent confirmed.

CC: loose stools for a few months.

Since about July: 3-4 loose stools a day, lots of bloating and gas, worse later in the day. Clothes looser, she thinks she's lost about 5 pounds without trying. Tired, though she blames back-to-school. Also an itchy rash on both elbows and the fronts of the knees, little blisters that she scratches open. No blood in stool, no fever, no vomiting. No travel, no antibiotics. Glucose readings more erratic, some lows after meals she didn't absorb.

On video: rash on elbows shown to camera, clusters of small excoriated papules and a few vesicles, symmetric. Appears thin but comfortable.

FH matters here: maternal aunt with celiac, she has T1DM.

A/P: chronic diarrhea with weight loss and a symmetric vesicular extensor rash in a T1DM pt with a family history of celiac. Celiac high on the list; the rash fits dermatitis herpetiformis. Referring to GI for serology and endoscopy rather than piecemeal testing here. Asked her NOT to start a gluten-free diet before GI sees her, it makes testing unreliable. Told her to let endo know about the post-meal lows. Will come in for flu shot next week.

documents.body: Influenza L arm, bivalent COVID booster R arm. Both tolerated. GI referral status checked for her: appointment 11/11 with outside GI.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY ASSOCIATES
New consult, seen 11/11/2022. Referred by her primary care physician for diarrhea and rash.

HPI: 28-year-old teacher with type 1 diabetes. Several months of loose stools, abdominal bloating and weight she did not intend to lose. She has noticed the bloating is clearly worse after bread or pasta. Persistent tiredness. Itchy, blistering rash over both elbows and knees.

PMH: type 1 diabetes (endocrinology). Heavy menstrual periods.
Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals by scale; ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for cramps.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with type 1 diabetes; mother with autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt with celiac disease.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, preschool teacher.

Exam: Weight 50 kg. Thin young woman, pale. Abdomen soft. Skin: clusters of tense small vesicles over the extensor elbows and knees, some excoriated.

Labs today: Hgb 9.8 g/dL, MCV 74 fL. Iron 30 mcg/dL, TIBC 450 mcg/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL. Tissue transglutaminase IgA sent, pending.

Impression:
1. Chronic diarrhea, bloating, weight loss with gluten-related symptoms, strong family and personal autoimmune history: celiac disease suspected; serology pending.
2. Rash typical of dermatitis herpetiformis.
3. Microcytic anemia with low iron indices.

Plan: We will call with the tTG. If positive, upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies. Please continue a normal gluten-containing diet until biopsies are taken. The anemia needs evaluation and iron replacement; we would appreciate your team managing this. Letter copied to patient.

Gastroenterology

She would prefer to schedule it during a school break; she understands she should keep eating gluten until then. Our schedulers will contact her.

documents.title: GI visit and your blood count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Lauren, I got the GI notes. Sorry about the celiac news, though it explains a lot, and it is very treatable. They also found your blood count is low and your iron stores are low, which likely accounts for some of the tiredness. I'd like to see you in the office to go over the anemia and start treatment. The front desk will reach out; early January is fine if December is hard with school.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 28F, T1DM, celiac by serology in November (EGD pending). Here about the low blood count GI found, and she is wiped out. Three months of getting steadily more tired, can't keep up on the playground the way she used to, gets lightheaded a lot, standing up or after recess, and is having a hard time focusing in the classroom by afternoon. Periods have been heavy since she was a teenager, nothing new there; still takes OTC ibuprofen for cramps. Admits she hasn't had a real check-up since early 2020. Eating has been whatever is fast: toast, tea, a can of soup most nights. Still eating gluten per GI. No black or bloody stools, no chest pain.

Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro per scale, ibuprofen 400 prn. NKDA.

O: HR 104, rest of vitals as charted. Thin. Conjunctivae pale. Heart regular, a soft systolic flow murmur at the left sternal border, no gallop. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. DRE with chaperone: brown stool, guaiac negative. Skin: elbow rash fading.
CBC in office: Hgb 9.1, Hct 28, MCV 71, RDW elevated.
GI iron studies 11/11 reviewed: iron 30, TIBC 450, ferritin 15.

A/P
1. Iron deficiency anemia, microcytic, symptomatic but stable. Causes: heavy menses plus celiac malabsorption, poor intake. Stool guaiac negative, no GI bleeding symptoms. Start ferrous sulfate 325 daily, with orange juice, away from tea and coffee. Mild resting tachycardia and flow murmur fit the anemia; ER precautions for chest pain, fainting.
2. Heavy menstrual bleeding - longstanding, contributing. Ibuprofen ok for now.
3. Celiac disease - EGD to be scheduled by GI.
4. Overdue for physical and Pap: booking March, will recheck CBC then.

documents.title: Iron pills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Picked up the iron. Is it better at night or morning? I take my long-acting insulin at bedtime if that matters.

documents.title: RE: Iron pills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Doesn't interact with your insulin. Morning on an empty stomach absorbs best, with some juice or vitamin C, but if it upsets your stomach it's fine with breakfast. Keep it two hours away from tea or coffee. It will turn your stool dark, that's expected.

documents.author: MA

A/P
1. IDA on oral iron, recheck CBC today.
2. Celiac - encouraged her to get the EGD on the calendar now for July so that the diet can start.
3. Heavy menses - unchanged.
4. HM: Pap today. Lipids, BMP. Flu/COVID in fall. HIV/HCV done 2019.
RTC after EGD or sooner.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY ASSOCIATES
Follow-up visit 07/07/2023, with upper endoscopy the same morning.

29-year-old with type 1 diabetes, celiac disease on serology since November 2022 and iron deficiency anemia found in January 2023, back for persistent GI symptoms and the planned endoscopy. Symptoms have been going on for roughly a year and clearly worse since early spring. Four to six loose bowel movements a day, bulky and foul-smelling, often a couple of hours after eating. Bloating with pasta, bread, pastries and some breakfast cereals. Fatigue and trouble concentrating. No fevers, no night sweats, no recent travel. Cycles regular, though flow has been heavier for several months. On and off mouth sores this past year that she put down to stress. Occasional vague aching in her bones. Nails more brittle. She has kept her diet unchanged as we asked, though she sometimes skips meals because of the bloating. Probiotics and a fiber supplement did not help.

ROS: no rash currently; on questioning remembers an itchy rash on the elbows last year that went away on its own. No joint swelling, back pain or visual change. No urinary symptoms or leg swelling.

Medications: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. NKDA.
Family history: father type 1 diabetes; mother autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt celiac. No inflammatory bowel disease or colon cancer in the family.
Social: preschool teacher, lives with her partner. No sick contacts, no hospital stays, no antibiotics in the past year. No pets. City water. Does not smoke; no alcohol or drugs.

Vitals: T 37.2 C, BP 108/66, P 78, RR 14. BMI 18.4.
Exam: alert, cooperative, thin. Mouth: one shallow, sharply bordered ulcer on the left buccal mucosa. Abdomen mildly distended, hyperactive bowel sounds, mild diffuse tenderness most in the upper abdomen; no organomegaly, no masses. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Labs 07/07: Hgb 10.8, MCV 74, ferritin 8. Liver enzymes normal. TSH normal. Stool culture and ova/parasite exam negative. Fecal leukocytes positive.

Procedure: EGD today, report attached. Scalloping of the duodenal folds; biopsies taken.

Impression: celiac disease, clinically and endoscopically active, with iron deficiency from malabsorption. Final plan after pathology.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Procedure: esophagogastroduodenoscopy with biopsies, 07/07/2023.
Indication: positive tissue transglutaminase IgA, diarrhea, iron deficiency anemia.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care. ASA II.
Findings: Esophagus normal. Stomach normal; no ulcers. Duodenum: scalloped appearance of the mucosal folds in the bulb and second portion. Four biopsies from the second portion and two from the bulb.
Complications: none. Estimated blood loss minimal.
Impression: duodenal scalloping, consistent with celiac disease. Await pathology.

reports.text:
Specimen A: duodenum, second portion, biopsies (4). Specimen B: duodenal bulb, biopsies (2).
Microscopic: small bowel mucosa with villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes. No granulomas, no dysplasia, no organisms identified.
reports.conclusion: Duodenal biopsies with villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes, consistent with celiac disease in the appropriate serologic context.

We will repeat tTG in about a year to gauge adherence. Follow-up in GI as needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP

29F, celiac (gluten-free since July), T1DM, IDA on ferrous sulfate since January.

GI side much better: one or two formed stools a day, bloating mostly gone, up about 2 kg. But still exhausted, short of breath on the stairs at school, dizzy when she stands quickly. Taking the iron daily, no GI side effects. Periods still heavy.

Exam: pale, conjunctival pallor. RRR, flow murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Labs today: Hgb 9.7, ferritin 9. Essentially no response after 10 months of oral iron.

A/P
1. IDA refractory to oral iron - malabsorption from celiac plus ongoing menstrual loss. Referring to hematology for IV iron. Continue oral iron in the meantime.
2. Celiac - improving on diet.
3. Heavy menses - ongoing.
Hematology referral sent; she prefers a late afternoon or a vacation-week appointment.

documents.title: Hematology Consultation
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Outside hematology and oncology practice. Consultation 01/01/2024 (holiday clinic session).
Reason: iron deficiency anemia with celiac disease, not responding to oral iron.

She tells us she still feels drained, gets winded with exertion and lightheaded if she stands up fast. Appetite has been poor. Celiac disease confirmed by biopsy in July; gluten-free since. Long history of heavy periods.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Arrival 06/26/2025 19:40. Discharged 22:05.

Chief complaint: right eye swelling.

HPI: 31-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, celiac disease and iron deficiency anemia, followed in GI and hematology clinics. Three days of pain, redness and swelling at the inner corner of the right eye with watery discharge, and her vision on that side is a little blurry. No fever, no injury, no recent illness. Diabetes well controlled on insulin per patient.

Meds: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin lispro with meals, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: never smoker, alcohol rarely, preschool teacher.

Vitals: afebrile, hemodynamically normal.
Exam: Right medial canthus: erythema and tenderness over the lacrimal sac; pressure over the sac expresses pus from the punctum. Visual acuity slightly reduced on the right compared with the left. No foreign body seen. Conjunctiva otherwise quiet, cornea clear, pupils equal and reactive, extraocular movements full and painless, no proptosis. Left eye normal.

MDM: presentation consistent with acute dacryocystitis of the right lacrimal sac, no signs of orbital involvement.

Disposition: discharged home. Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg by mouth twice daily for 10 days. Warm compresses with gentle massage four times a day. Ophthalmology follow-up within a few days; return for fever, worsening swelling, eye pain with movement or further vision loss. Glucose checks as usual. Copy to PCP.

Exam: afebrile. Right medial canthus with mild residual redness, minimal tenderness, no fluctuance, no discharge expressed today. Eye movements full and painless. Conjunctiva quiet. Vision grossly equal.

A/P: Acute dacryocystitis, right, improving on oral antibiotic. Finish the 10 days, warm compresses. ED asked for ophthalmology follow-up: referral placed, office reached and seeing her Thursday. Return precautions reviewed.
